disable_telemetry: Windows constantly collects data about how you use your PC and sends it to Microsoft. This tweak cuts that to the minimum. For example, the background "collector" that sometimes loads the CPU right in the middle of a game stops running.
disable_web_search: When you search in Start, Windows also sends the query to the internet and shows Bing results. This tweak keeps search on your PC only. For example, type "steam" and Steam shows up right away instead of a website opening in the browser.
disable_activity_history: Windows remembers which apps and files you opened and may send that history to Microsoft. This tweak turns it off. For example, the recent files timeline disappears from Task View (Win+Tab).
disable_error_reporting: When an app crashes, Windows builds a report and sends it to Microsoft. You get nothing out of it. This tweak turns it off: no more "Checking for a solution" window hanging around after a game crash.
disable_telemetry_tasks: Windows runs scheduled tasks that collect data about your apps, drives and USB sticks. One of them sometimes loads the CPU and disk for a couple of minutes. For example, a game suddenly starts stuttering and Task Manager shows "Microsoft Compatibility Telemetry". This tweak turns those tasks off.
disable_copilot: Removes the Copilot AI assistant and its taskbar button. If you don't use it, that's less clutter in the system and on the taskbar.
disable_cortana: Turns off the Cortana voice assistant: it doesn't start in the background or collect data. Regular search in Start works as before. Cortana is already gone in Windows 11, so there the tweak changes nothing.
disable_promo_app_installs: Windows installs "recommended" apps by itself, like Candy Crush and social networks, and shows ads and "fun facts" on the lock screen. This tweak stops that. For example, after an update, games you never installed won't show up in Start. Apps already installed stay.
disable_widgets: Removes Windows 11 widgets: the news and weather panel on the left of the taskbar that runs in the background. For example, the news feed stops popping up when your mouse drifts to the screen corner.
disable_transparency: Removes the see-through effects in Start, the taskbar and windows. A bit less work for the GPU, and text on panels reads more clearly.
disable_window_animations: Windows open, minimize and close instantly, without smooth animations. For example, press minimize and the window is gone at once instead of sliding down. Most noticeable on slower PCs.
faster_menus: Submenus open right away instead of after half a second. For example, hover over "Send to" in the right-click menu and the list appears instantly.
disable_sticky_keys_prompt: Press Shift five times fast in a game and Windows throws you to the desktop with a "Turn on Sticky Keys?" window. This tweak removes that window.
high_performance_power: Turns on the hidden Ultimate Performance power plan: the CPU doesn't drop its clock to save power and responds without delay. For example, less micro-stutter when the load in a game spikes. The PC uses more power, and a laptop battery drains faster. Turning it off brings back your previous plan.
disable_startup_delay: After you sign in, startup apps don't launch right away but after an artificial delay. This tweak removes it. For example, Discord and Steam open as soon as the desktop appears.
disable_background_apps: Microsoft Store apps (Mail, Weather, Xbox and others) don't run in the background when closed. That saves memory and CPU. Downside: these apps may stop showing notifications, for example about new emails in the built-in Mail app.
disable_sysmain: The SysMain service preloads apps you often open into memory. On an SSD it barely helps, and on slower PCs it's a common cause of "Disk at 100%". For example, if everything lags for a couple of minutes after boot, this is often why. If Windows is on a regular hard drive (HDD), better leave it on: apps will open more slowly.
disable_search_indexing: Windows constantly goes through the files on your drive to make search faster. That loads the disk and CPU, sometimes right during a game. Downside: file search in Start and Explorer gets slower, and it may stop working in Outlook.
disable_edge_background: Edge starts with Windows and stays in memory even after you close it, so it can open faster later. This tweak blocks that. For example, if you use Chrome, Edge stops quietly taking up memory.
disable_power_throttling: Windows deliberately slows down background apps to save power. Sometimes it slows down what you need, like Discord or OBS recording while you play. This tweak turns that off. A laptop battery drains faster.
disable_unneeded_services: Turns off services almost nobody needs: fax, the retail store demo mode, push message routing and Windows Media Player library sharing. For example, if you don't have a fax, its service just sits in memory for nothing.
disable_maps_updates: Windows downloads updates for the Maps app by itself. If you don't use offline maps (almost nobody does), that's extra background downloads. This tweak turns them off.
disable_xbox_services: Turns off Xbox services: Xbox Live sign-in, cloud saves and Xbox networking. If you play on Steam, Epic or Riot, you don't need them. Don't turn them off if you play through the Xbox app or Game Pass, or use Xbox accessories.
disable_game_dvr: Xbox Game Bar constantly records your game in the background so you can save the last seconds. That loads the GPU even if you never save anything and costs a few FPS. This tweak turns off background recording. OBS and NVIDIA ShadowPlay work as before.
disable_mouse_acceleration: Turns off "Enhance pointer precision". With it on, a fast mouse movement sends the cursor further than a slow one over the same distance. For example, in a shooter a quick flick overshoots the head. Without acceleration, your crosshair moves exactly as far as you move the mouse.
keyboard_fast_repeat: When you hold a key, Windows waits half a second before repeating it. This tweak halves the delay and sets the fastest repeat rate. For example, arrow keys and Backspace in text get noticeably faster. In games held keys don't change: response there is already instant.
enable_game_mode: During a game, Windows postpones updates and notifications and gives the game more resources. For example, an update won't start installing mid-match. The mode is usually already on: the tweak checks and turns it on if it's off.
foreground_priority: The app you're in right now (a game, for example) gets more CPU time than what runs in the background. For example, a browser with lots of tabs takes less away from the game.
mmcss_games: Windows has a service that splits resources between games, video and audio. This tweak tells it to give games high priority and leave background tasks 10% instead of 20%. For example, Windows background work gets in the way of your game less.
enable_hags: The GPU manages its own memory and frame queue instead of the CPU. Slightly lower latency and CPU load, and newer games need it for DLSS Frame Generation. Requires an NVIDIA GTX 10xx, AMD RX 5000 or newer GPU and a recent driver.
no_auto_reboot_after_update: Windows no longer restarts the PC by itself while you're using it. For example, no more stepping away for a minute and coming back to a closed game and an update installing. Updates install as usual, and you restart when it suits you. Settings will show "Some settings are managed by your organization", which is normal. May not work on Windows Home.
disable_delivery_optimization: Windows shares downloaded updates with other computers over your internet connection, like a torrent. That eats bandwidth and can raise your ping in games. This tweak turns sharing off: updates download only from Microsoft servers.
